propositions: Implement a single durable last-pass writer that records reconciler pass outcome before releasing the lock, advancing refs/reconciler/last-pass via CAS with three bounded retry attempts and 100/200 ms backoff on mismatch.

Canonical rebar bridge status and hidden rebar bridge-status commands must expose identical read-only verdicts with precedence PAUSED > RUNNING > FOREIGN > FAILED > STALE > HEALTHY, where NEVER_RUN applies only without both record and live lock, and status makes no mutations or lease steals.

Local writer and status must derive stable local:<repo-env-id> identity from .env-id, while explicit REBAR_ENV_ID wins; missing or unreadable .env-id is a hard configuration error; canary explicitly targets reconciler identity unchanged from workflow supply.

Canary detects CRASHED via two read-only live-fence snapshots across the lock-held lease, rejects observed leases over 480 seconds before the fixed ten-minute budget, and moves from GitHub Actions heartbeat polling to durable status ref while retaining one-release explicit REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE=github-api rollback.

Duplicate pass-record producers must be removed after semantic and string reference sweeps; rich detail resides in one rolling .tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/last-pass.json file committed by the normal tickets-branch path and safely degrades when absent or mismatched.

All acceptance criteria including parity of canonical and legacy commands, exact verdict and exit contracts, identity isolation, producer CAS behavior, detail rolling degradation, two-snapshot crash detection, canary ref fetch with no canonical heartbeat query, ADR 0094 numbering convention compliance, and RED-first held-out oracle are proven GREEN in test suites and CI.
